jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: South Korea is one of the few countries with a comprehensive AI statute: the Framework Act on the Development of AI and Establishment of a Foundation of Trust (AI Basic Act), promulgated in January 2025 and in force since 22 January 2026, with an Enforcement Decree setting obligations for high-impact AI, transparency and labelling of generative AI, and safety duties for models above a 10^26 FLOP compute threshold. The Ministry of Science and ICT leads implementation through guidelines on high-impact AI, impact assessment and transparency, alongside national AI ethics principles (2026), the Digital Bill of Rights (2023) and AI security guides, while the presidential National AI Strategy Committee sets strategy. Public-sector AI is governed by the 2026 Act on AI- and Data-based Administration and Ministry of the Interior and Safety ethics standards. The Personal Information Protection Commission enforces automated-decision rights under the Personal Information Protection Act and has issued detailed AI guidance and decisions on chatbots, large language models and DeepSeek. Financial, medical, communications, education and copyright regulators add sector rules, and all 17 metropolitan and provincial governments have AI ordinances.
lead_institutions: Ministry of the Interior and Safety
Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service
Ministry of Food and Drug Safety
Korea Communications Commission (now Korea Media and Communications Commission)
Metropolitan and provincial governments (Seoul, Gyeonggi, Busan and others)
narrative.review_notes: Deep review completed on 8 October 2026, covering national laws and decrees, central government (the Ministry of Science and ICT, the national AI strategy committee, the AI Safety Institute and the Ministry of the Interior and Safety), the Personal Information Protection Commission, sector regulators (finance, food and drug safety, communications, education, human rights, copyright and transport), and all 17 metropolitan and provincial governments. Searches were made in Korean and English. The Digital Platform Government Committee website could not be reached, and some privacy commission decisions are available only as press releases. Pending: a draft guideline on the safety of frontier AI, which so far is available only on an industry association's website and not on a government page; the full text of the national AI action plan (AI Basic Plan 2026-2028), further ministry notices under the AI Basic Act on safety obligations and compute calculation, public-sector AI guides from the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, and AI policies of city, county and district governments.

instruments.english_title: Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust (Presidential Decree No. 36053)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Korea (Presidential Decree; competent ministry: Ministry of Science and ICT)
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)
instruments.current_status: Presidential Decree No. 36053, promulgated 21 January 2026, in force 22 January 2026 (Annex 1 digital medical device part from 24 January 2026); it repealed the Regulation on the Establishment and Operation of the National AI Strategy Committee and transferred that committee to the Act. Amended by Decree No. 36506 of 20 July 2026 (in force 21 July 2026: scope of AI-vulnerable groups, usage-cost support, AI research institutes, implementing Act No. 21311) and by Decree No. 36580 of 18 August 2026 (Enforcement Decree of the National R&D Innovation Act, cross-reference only; in force 20 August 2026). Current version in force since 20 August 2026. No separate Enforcement Rule (시행규칙) of the Act found on law.go.kr. Official English translation of Decree No. 36053 published on law.go.kr. The MSIT notices on compute calculation (Art. 24(2)) and safety-duty implementation (Act Art. 32(3)) were not found on law.go.kr as of 8 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Implements the AI Basic Act: it organises the National AI Strategy Committee and its support group, designates the AI Policy Center and AI Safety Institute, and sets procedures for AI clusters, training-data support and the Korea AI Promotion Association. It specifies how operators give prior notice of high-impact or generative AI and label generative outputs (human-readable or machine-readable with at least one notice), with exemptions for obvious or internal use (Art. 23); sets the Art. 32 safety-duty threshold as systems trained with at least 10^26 floating-point operations that also use frontier technology and pose broad, serious risk to life, safety or fundamental rights (Art. 24); and sets the high-impact AI confirmation procedure, operator duties, impact assessment, domestic-agent thresholds and the fine schedule (KRW 5-15 million for missing notice, 20 million for no domestic agent, 10-30 million for ignoring orders; Annex 2). Annex 1 deems compliance with sector laws (digital medical devices, autonomous vehicles, credit-information explanation duties, etc.) as meeting certain high-impact duties.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (binding-law, government-governance, risk-assurance, transparency, generative-ai).

instruments.official_title: 인공지능 및 데이터 기반 행정 활성화에 관한 법률
instruments.english_title: Act on the Promotion of Artificial Intelligence- and Data-Based Administration (formerly Act on the Promotion of Data-Based Administration; Act No. 17370)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)
instruments.current_status: Enacted as the Act on the Promotion of Data-Based Administration (데이터기반행정 활성화에 관한 법률), Act No. 17370, promulgated 9 June 2020, in force 10 December 2020. Renamed and extended to AI by Act No. 21392 of 27 February 2026, in force 28 August 2026, except Art. 32 (public-sector AI impact assessment) in force 28 February 2027. Competent ministry: Ministry of the Interior and Safety. Official English translation on law.go.kr covers only the pre-2026 version (Act on the Promotion of Data-Based Administration).
instruments.summary: Governs the use of data and, since the 2026 amendment, AI by public institutions: it defines AI-based administration and requires public institutions using AI for policy or decisions to retain final authority and responsibility and to consider bias and transparency (Art. 3). Public institutions must train staff in AI, keep training data at adequate quality and report an inventory of their AI-enabled services (type, purpose, data), which the Minister of the Interior and Safety publishes annually (Arts. 28-30); the Minister must issue public-sector AI ethics standards (Art. 31). From 28 February 2027, public institutions must assess the impact on fundamental rights before introducing AI, publish the results and adopt risk-management plans, with limited exemptions (Art. 32).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (binding-law, public-sector, risk-assurance, transparency, ethics).

instruments.official_title: 인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법
instruments.english_title: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Creation of a Foundation for Trust (AI Basic Act; Act No. 20676)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)
instruments.current_status: Act No. 20676, promulgated 21 January 2025, in force 22 January 2026 (Supplementary Provisions Art. 1: one year after promulgation; the digital medical device part of Art. 2(4)(d) from 24 January 2026). Amended by Act No. 21065 (Government Organization Act, 1 October 2025; Statistics Korea renamed) and by Act No. 21311 of 20 January 2026 (National AI Committee renamed National AI Strategy Committee and enlarged to 60 members; training-data definition; AI-vulnerable groups; AI research institutes; venture fund support; procurement preference), in force 22 January 2026 with Arts. 3(5), 6(2)(7)-(8), 17-2, 18, 22-3 and 35(1) second sentence in force 21 July 2026. Current consolidated version on law.go.kr effective 21 July 2026. Official English translation published on law.go.kr (Korea Legislation Research Institute) for Acts No. 20676 and 21311. No statutory grace period for fines found in the Act; any non-enforcement period announced by MSIT is administrative and not recorded here. A further amendment bill (No. 2219835, on Art. 31 labelling exceptions) is pending in the National Assembly (lead).
instruments.summary: Korea's framework AI law: it requires a three-yearly AI Basic Plan, establishes the National AI Strategy Committee under the President, the AI Policy Center and the AI Safety Institute, and sets support measures (training data, AI clusters, SMEs, start-ups, procurement preference for AI products by state bodies). AI business operators must give prior notice when products use high-impact or generative AI, label generative-AI outputs and clearly disclose realistic synthetic sound, image or video (Art. 31); operators of systems above a compute threshold set by decree must identify, assess and mitigate lifecycle risks and report to MSIT (Art. 32); high-impact AI (used in energy supply, drinking water, health care, medical devices, nuclear safety, biometric analysis for criminal investigation, hiring and loan screening, transport, public-sector eligibility decisions and school student assessment) carries risk-management, explanation, user-protection, human-oversight and documentation duties, and operators must endeavour to assess impacts on fundamental rights (Arts. 33-35). Foreign operators meeting decree thresholds must appoint a domestic agent (Art. 36); MSIT may investigate and order corrections, with administrative fines up to KRW 30 million (Art. 43); it does not apply to AI used solely for national defence or security.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (binding-law, government-governance, risk-assurance, transparency, generative-ai).

instruments.official_title: 인공지능제품ㆍ서비스 확인 절차 운영에 관한 고시
instruments.english_title: Notice on the Operation of the Confirmation Procedure for AI Products and Services (MSIT Notice No. 2026-50)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science and ICT
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)
instruments.current_status: MSIT Notice No. 2026-50, issued and in force 21 July 2026 (enactment); responsible office: MSIT AI Safety and Trust Policy Division. Current as of 8 October 2026. It is the only MSIT notice under the AI Basic Act found on law.go.kr.
instruments.summary: Issued under Art. 16(3) of the AI Basic Act and Art. 15(4)(1) of its Enforcement Decree, it sets the procedure for confirming that a product or service uses AI, which supports the Act's preference for AI products in public procurement. Applicants (who must first obtain a Public Procurement Service catalogue number) apply to the Korea AI Promotion Association, which has the Telecommunications Technology Association carry out a technical review against seven criteria (an AI processing system that learns or infers, meaningful outputs, a clear place in the product architecture, working main functions, verifiable API calls for external models). The Association decides within 15 days (extendable by 30), issues a confirmation certificate, and must revoke confirmations obtained by fraud.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (binding-law, procurement).

instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Korea (Presidential Decree; competent ministry: Ministry of the Interior and Safety)
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)

instruments.summary: Implements the Act on AI- and data-based administration: it sets planning procedures, data registration and sharing rules, and the appointment of AI and data-based administration officers and their council chaired by the Vice-Minister of the Interior and Safety. The 2026 amendment adds the procedure for licensing the Public AI and Data Association and, from 28 February 2027, the criteria and procedure for public-sector AI impact assessments (considering transparency of AI decision-making and reliability of results), exemptions confirmed by the Minister (e.g. pilots of up to one year in a limited scope) and the content of risk-management plans (system structure, performance and safety checks, suspension and user-protection rules).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (binding-law, public-sector, risk-assurance).

instruments.official_title: 개인정보 보호법
instruments.english_title: Personal Information Protection Act (Act No. 10465)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)
instruments.current_status: Act No. 10465, promulgated 29 March 2011, in force 30 September 2011. Art. 37-2 (automated decisions) inserted by Act No. 19234 of 14 March 2023 and in force 15 March 2024 (one year after promulgation). Latest amendment Act No. 21445 of 10 March 2026, in force 11 September 2026 (some provisions 1 July 2027). Competent authority: Personal Information Protection Commission. Official English translation on law.go.kr. PIPC guidance on AI is covered separately.
instruments.summary: Korea's general data protection law, binding all personal information controllers and governing the processing of personal data for AI training and use, enforced by the Personal Information Protection Commission. Art. 37-2 (added in 2023) gives data subjects the right to refuse a fully automated decision, including by systems applying AI, that significantly affects their rights or obligations (except decisions based on consent, law or contract), and to request an explanation; controllers must stop applying the decision or provide human re-processing or explanation, and must publish the criteria and procedures of automated decisions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (data-privacy, binding-law, transparency).

instruments.official_title: 공직선거법
instruments.english_title: Public Official Election Act (Act No. 4739)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)
instruments.current_status: Act No. 4739, promulgated and in force 16 March 1994. Art. 82-8 (deepfake campaigning) inserted by Act No. 19855 of 28 December 2023, in force 29 January 2024 (one month after promulgation). Latest amendment Act No. 22052 of 29 September 2026, in force 2 October 2026. Administered by the National Election Commission. Official English translation on law.go.kr (earlier version).
instruments.summary: Korea's election law for presidential, National Assembly and local elections. Art. 82-8 (added in 2023) bans producing, editing, distributing, screening or posting deepfakes (realistic virtual sound, images or video made with AI technology) for election campaigning from 90 days before election day, and outside that period requires such content to be clearly labelled as AI-generated as prescribed by National Election Commission rules. Art. 255(5) (up to seven years' imprisonment) and Art. 250(4) attach criminal penalties, including heavier penalties where unlabelled deepfakes are used to publish false facts.

instruments.official_title: 성폭력범죄의 처벌 등에 관한 특례법
instruments.english_title: Act on Special Cases concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes (Act No. 11556)
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)
instruments.current_status: Wholly amended by Act No. 11556 of 18 December 2012, in force 19 June 2013 (six months after promulgation). Art. 14-2 inserted by Act No. 17086 of 24 March 2020 (in force 25 June 2020); amended by Act No. 20459 of 16 October 2024, in force that day (possession/viewing offence, higher penalties). Latest amendment Act No. 21997 of 29 September 2026, in force 2 October 2026. Competent ministry: Ministry of Justice. Official English translation on law.go.kr (earlier version).
instruments.summary: Criminal law on sexual offences. Art. 14-2 (added in 2020 and strengthened in 2024) criminalises editing, synthesising or processing a person's face, body or voice into sexually explicit material against their will (sexual deepfakes) and distributing it, with up to seven years' imprisonment; distribution for profit over networks carries at least three years. The 2024 amendment also made possessing, purchasing, storing or viewing such material punishable by up to three years' imprisonment.

instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)
instruments.current_status: Wholly amended (from the Framework Act on National Informatization) by Act No. 17344 of 9 June 2020, in force 10 December 2020 (six months after promulgation). Latest change by Act No. 20672 of 21 January 2025 (Digital Inclusion Act consequential amendment), in force 22 January 2026. Competent ministry: Ministry of Science and ICT. Official English translation on law.go.kr.
instruments.summary: Framework law on the 'intelligent information society', covering intelligent information technologies (including technologies that implement learning, reasoning and judgement electronically). It requires a comprehensive plan, establishes the National Information Society Agency (NIA), allows the State and local governments to carry out social impact assessments of widely used intelligent information services covering safety, reliability, privacy and ethics, with MSIT able to publish results and recommend measures (Art. 56), and requires state bodies to establish intelligent-information-society ethics based on publicness, accountability, controllability and transparency (Art. 62).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (binding-law, ethics, risk-assurance, government-governance).

instruments.summary: Governs electronic government services and information systems of administrative bodies. Art. 18-2 (intelligent e-government services, added in 2021) allows administrative bodies to deliver e-government services using AI and similar technologies and lets the Minister of the Interior and Safety provide administrative, financial and technical support, with details set by presidential decree and the rules of the National Assembly, courts, Constitutional Court and National Election Commission.

instruments.current_status: Act No. 21759, promulgated 9 June 2026; enters into force 10 March 2027 (listed as scheduled for enforcement on law.go.kr). Competent ministry: Ministry of Science and ICT.
instruments.summary: Sets a support framework for AI data centres: a basic plan, a dedicated agency, an industry association, surveys and statistics, and a duty for AI data centre operators to report their location and purpose to MSIT. It provides one-stop processing of permits, priority infrastructure, exemption from power-grid impact assessment for centres outside the capital region, special cases under building, industrial-site and port laws, and AI data centre special zones outside the capital region.

Competent ministry: 산업통상부. Official English translation on law.go.kr covers only the pre-2026 title.
instruments.summary: Promotes digital transformation and AI use in industry: it defines industrial AI and its supplier and user companies, requires a comprehensive plan for industrial digital transformation and AI use, and establishes a committee and support centre for the purpose. It also governs industrial data use, specialised companies and lead projects, together with an industrial AI data centre provision (Art. 24-2), standardisation, regulatory-improvement support and financial and tax support.

instruments.english_title: Regulation on the Establishment and Operation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy Committee (Presidential Decree No. 35735)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Korea (Presidential Decree; competent ministry: Ministry of Science and ICT)
instruments.publisher_name: National Law Information Center (Ministry of Government Legislation)

instruments.summary: Replaced the National AI Committee with the National AI Strategy Committee under the President, to deliberate and decide on the national AI vision and mid- to long-term strategy, inter-ministerial coordination of AI policies and projects, and implementation checks and performance management. It set the committee's membership, support group and secondments.

instruments.official_title: 인공지능 국가전략
instruments.english_title: National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (December 2019)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science and ICT (with relevant ministries; joint government strategy)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science and ICT
instruments.current_status: Announced at the 53rd Cabinet Meeting chaired by the President on 17 December 2019 (MSIT press release of the same day, with the strategy PDF attached). Kept as historical: Korea's national AI direction has since been reset by the AI Basic Act (in force 22 January 2026) and the Korea AI Action Plan adopted as the statutory AI Basic Plan 2026-2028 on 25 February 2026; no official text formally repealing the 2019 strategy was found, so lifecycle 'superseded' reflects replacement by later national plans.
instruments.summary: Korea's first whole-of-government AI strategy, prepared by MSIT with all ministries under the vision 'Beyond an IT powerhouse to an AI powerhouse'. It set 2030 targets (3rd in the world in digital competitiveness, up to KRW 455 trillion in economic effect from AI, 10th in quality of life) and organised 100 action tasks under 9 strategies in 3 areas: a world-leading AI ecosystem (data, computing, regulation), using AI well (talent, AI across industry, digital government), and people-centred AI (jobs safety net, prevention of AI dysfunction and AI ethics).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (historical, strategy).

instruments.official_title: 사람이 중심이 되는 인공지능(AI) 윤리기준
instruments.english_title: Human-centred National Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence (AI) Ethics (2020)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science and ICT and Korea Information Society Development Institute (relevant ministries jointly)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science and ICT
instruments.current_status: Adopted at the plenary meeting of the Presidential Committee on the Fourth Industrial Revolution on 23 December 2020 after a draft (27 November 2020) and public hearing (7 December 2020). The text states it is a moral, self-regulatory norm and not a binding law or guideline. Succeeded by the 대한민국 인공지능 윤리원칙 (Korea AI Ethics Principles) of 21 August 2026, which MSIT states 'inherits' the 2020 standard while reflecting the AI Basic Act.
instruments.summary: Korea's national AI ethics standard, setting 'Humanity' as the highest value with 3 basic principles (human dignity, the public good of society, purposefulness of technology) and 10 key requirements (human rights, privacy, respect for diversity, prohibition of harm, publicness, solidarity, data management, accountability, safety, transparency). It applies to all members of society—government and public bodies, developers, providers and users—across the AI life cycle, as a voluntary, non-binding platform from which sector-specific norms and self-checklists were later developed.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (ethics, historical).

instruments.official_title: 디지털 공동번영사회의 가치와 원칙에 관한 헌장 : 디지털 권리장전
instruments.english_title: Charter on the Values and Principles of a Digital Society of Shared Prosperity: Digital Bill of Rights
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science and ICT
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science and ICT
instruments.current_status: Published by MSIT on 25 September 2023 (date on the official policy page). A declaratory charter proposed to the international community; it creates no legal obligations. MSIT planned follow-up legislation (including an AI act) in line with it.
instruments.summary: A declaratory charter setting out Korea's vision for a new digital order, in a preamble and 28 articles in 6 chapters: basic principles (freedom and rights, fair access, safety and trust, innovation, human welfare), freedom and rights in the digital environment (access, expression, diversity, control of personal information, a right to non-digital alternatives in public services), fair access, a safe and trustworthy digital society, innovation and international solidarity. Art. 17 requires digital technology to be developed and used ethically and responsibly so as to secure safety and trust, and Art. 18 requires digital risks to be prevented and managed with transparent disclosure.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (ethics, government-governance).

instruments.official_title: 대한민국 인공지능 윤리원칙
instruments.english_title: Korea AI Ethics Principles (Republic of Korea Artificial Intelligence Ethics Principles, 2026)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science and ICT (relevant ministries jointly; with Korea Information Society Development Institute)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Science and ICT
instruments.current_status: Deliberated and confirmed at the 12th Ministerial Meeting on Science and Technology on 21 August 2026 and published by MSIT on 24 August 2026 (policy page with the 23-page PDF). Made under Art. 27 of the AI Basic Act. Draft published for comment 29 May 2026 (comments 29 May-8 July, 116; further comments 10-19 August, 37). Self-practice principles, not binding; MSIT plans a casebook commentary, sector self-checklists and education materials.
instruments.summary: National AI ethics principles made under Art. 27 of the AI Basic Act, applying to all areas of society and serving as the basis for sector ethics standards and guidelines. They set 3 values (human dignity, the public good of society, sustainability of humankind) and 7 principles (human-centredness, privacy protection, fairness and inclusiveness, accountability, safety, reliability, transparency), each with roles for providers, users, and government and society across the AI life cycle. They replace the 2020 AI Ethics Guidelines and stress that users, not only providers, are responsible actors, and that actors with greater AI capacity bear correspondingly greater responsibility.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Korean national instrument shaping AI governance (ethics).

instruments.official_title: 고영향 인공지능 판단 가이드라인
instruments.english_title: Guidelines for Determining High-Impact Artificial Intelligence (AI Basic Act)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Science and ICT

instruments.current_status: Issued by MSIT under Art. 33(3) of the AI Basic Act (MSIT may establish and disseminate guidelines on the criteria and examples of high-impact AI). instruments.summary: Explains how operators decide whether an AI system is 'high-impact AI' under the AI Basic Act, using a two-step test: (1) use in one of the statutory areas (energy supply, drinking water production, health care, medical and digital medical devices, nuclear materials and facilities, biometric analysis for criminal investigation or arrest, hiring and loan screening and similar decisions on individual rights, transport, public-service decisions by state bodies, and student assessment in early-childhood, primary and secondary education), and (2) whether the system may significantly affect or endanger life, physical safety or fundamental rights. coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: Backfill run 2026-10-08 in five parts (laws; central government; PIPC privacy; sector regulators; metropolitan and provincial governments). The run was interrupted once by a usage limit before any fragment was written; the resumed agents built every record from the official texts (law.go.kr API and ministry PDFs), re-reading earlier downloads before use, so no record written before the restart remained unchecked. law.go.kr Open API (DRF) began refusing requests mid-run (requires caller IP registration); the website was used instead. pipc.go.kr and law.go.kr intermittently reset curl connections (retried; PIPC page also confirmed via WebFetch). PIPC decision documents open only through a POST popup, so decisions cite official press-release pages. dpg.go.kr (Digital Platform Government Committee) refused proxy connections. The AI Basic Act implementation guideline PDFs are hosted by the AI Basic Act Support Desk of the Korea AI Software Industry Association (KOSA). Under the PROTOCOL §1 third-party-host rule, the four guidelines issued at commencement cite MSIT's 21 January 2026 press release (nttSeqNo 3186786, which names www.sw.or.kr as where they are published; the 28 January FAQ, nttSeqNo 3186809, says all guidelines are downloadable there) as source_url, with the KOSA file as official_pdf_url. The August 2026 draft frontier-AI safety guideline is offered only on the KOSA site and no MSIT page names that host for it, so it was moved to leads. MSIT press-release searches for 안전성 확보, 프런티어/프론티어, 지원 창구, 인공지능 기본법, 고영향 found no such page. No draft or consultation instrument remains recorded; the drafts category is closed with the pending AI Basic Act amendment bills and the frontier draft held as leads. kcc.go.kr now redirects to kmcc.go.kr. Seoul city ordinances are found through legal.seoul.go.kr, which links to the law.go.kr texts.
